packs.title: Bay, Hills and Pacific
packs.promise: Explore San Francisco through its bridge, island, art and ocean.

q.s: Look for evidence of different chapters in a place.
st: Follow the arrival orientation and current open visitor route.
Find two official interpretation details about different periods of island history.
Record the periods and a question connecting them.

q.s: Notice how a small change of position alters a winding view.
st: Check the public pedestrian route and choose a comfortable short section.
Move between two safe stopping positions clear of driveways.
Compare how a curve appears from each.

q.s: Build an original palette from architectural color.
st: Observe the houses from a public park or sidewalk position.
Choose three exterior colors or tonal contrasts.
Sketch an imaginary house or describe it in three sentences, using your colors in a different arrangement.

packs.title: Garden Intervals
packs.promise: Find small patterns between the park’s gardens.

q.s: Find three forms in a garden bed.
st: Stay on the open path outside the garden bed.
Find one round form, one repeated line and one change of texture; leaves, stems, supports and soil can count.
Record the three forms without picking or touching plants.

q.s: Test what stays in mind after a closer look.
st: From an open path, study one attached leaf for fifteen seconds without touching it.
Look away and write three features you remember, such as its edge, veins or position.
Look back and record one match or correction. No species name is needed.

q.s: Match visible features to ways people can use a place.
st: From an open walkway, find a tree, a path edge and a clear place to pause; substitute another visible feature if one is unavailable.
Match your three features to three possible jobs: offer shade, guide movement and make room for a pause.
Explain one match using something you can see. These are your choices, so a different match can work.

packs.title: Bay Stories
packs.promise: Read the bay through clocks, streetcars, small details, and your own stories.

q.s: Find something that carries, something that guides, and something that holds.
st: Choose a public resting spot with waterfront structures in view.
Find three features that appear to carry, guide, or hold something: a vessel, a railing, a dock edge, a path, a light, or another visible detail.
For each feature, write the visible evidence for your guess. It is fine to leave a function uncertain.
Save the three observations and mark the one you would like to learn more about.

q.t: A Book Cover for North Beach
q.s: Turn a square’s shapes into the cover of a book that does not exist yet.
st: Choose an open park path or resting spot with nearby buildings and greenery in view.
Pick a foreground shape, a background shape, and one small accent of color for an imaginary book cover.
Invent a title and one sentence about the story those three details suggest. Make it your own fiction, not a claim about the neighborhood.
Save the cover description in a field note or one photo with your title and sentence.

q.s: Let a short ride change the scene three times.
st: Check the posted F-line direction, fare and accessible boarding information before entering a boarding area.
Choose a short ride between suitable stops, or observe from an accessible public resting place beside the route.
Collect three changes in shape, color, or movement as the streetcar or the view passes. A particular car or livery is never required.
After alighting safely, save your three changes and choose the best final frame.
